questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Reducing your ability to focus on the road.
Decreasing your chances of an accident.
Making you fall asleep while driving.
Making you more aware of other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reducing your ability to focus on the road.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions affect your driving ability. If you are worried, excited, afraid, angry, or sad, you may not drive well. Stress reduces your focus on driving. It is better to wait to drive than to drive when you are emotionally upset.

questions.question: Before you start the engine, you should:

options.text: Make sure only back seat passengers have their seat belts on.
Make sure only adult passengers have their seat belts on.
Make sure only child passengers have their seat belts on.
Make sure all passengers have their seat belts on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure all passengers have their seat belts on.
questions.explanation: Get in the habit of fastening your seat belt and checking that all passengers do the same before you start the engine.

questions.question: When you borrow an unfamiliar vehicle from a friend, you should:

options.text: Not worry about it because all vehicles work the same way.
Not tell your friend that you are unfamiliar with the vehicle.
Ignore any problems to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Take a few minutes to learn where everything is and how to use all the vehicle's controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to learn where everything is and how to use all the vehicle's controls.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, spend a few minutes learning where and how to use the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, windshield wipers, brakes, gear selector, and horn. Fix any problems before you drive.

questions.question: To stay safe when crossing railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Look both ways only when the red light is flashing.
Listen and look both ways, then go only if it is safe.
Cross quickly when a train is coming.
Drive quickly under any lowering gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen and look both ways, then go only if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Look and listen for a train coming from either direction before crossing the tracks. Watch for warning signals and never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You are entering a one-way street the wrong way.
School crossing ahead.
Do not drive in this lane.
Drivers turning left on the green light must wait for oncoming traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers turning left on the green light must wait for oncoming traffic to pass.
questions.explanation: This sign is used with a traffic light to tell drivers that left-turning traffic does not have the right of way. Left-turning drivers must wait for oncoming traffic to clear before turning.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Two-way traffic.
Lane shifting.
Low clearance.
Added lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you that traffic may be coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: A driver taking an over-the-counter drug should:

options.text: Read the label before driving.
Drink alcohol instead.
Keep driving no matter what the label says.
Drive only during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the label before driving.
questions.explanation: Many over-the-counter medicines can affect your driving ability. Check the label of any medication you take, even cold or allergy medicine, for warnings. If you are unsure, ask your doctor or pharmacist if it is safe to drive while taking the medication.

questions.question: You should check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder when:

options.text: Pulling toward or away from a curb.
Turning left or right.
Changing lanes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Check your blind spot every time you change your vehicle's position. This includes turning, changing lanes, and pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: T intersection ahead.
Lane shifting.
Side road.
Do not block intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: T intersection ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you that a T intersection is coming and you may need to turn left or right.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the interstate, you should:

options.text: Cut quickly across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and take the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and take the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a sudden turn at the last moment to catch your exit. If you miss your exit, continue to the next one.

questions.question: If a police officer stops you, you should:

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and roll down your window.
Get your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.
Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
Get out and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the wheel when stopped by police. Tell passengers to keep their hands visible. Stay in your car unless the officer asks you to get out. Wait for the officer to ask for your driver's license, registration, and insurance information.

questions.question: A sign that a driver may be drunk is:

options.text: They weave between lanes.
They drive slower than normal traffic.
They make sudden or jerky stops.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include speeding, weaving between lanes, driving slower than normal traffic, making jerky movements, and making sudden stops.

questions.question: Distracted driving can be caused by:

options.text: Eating, drinking, or smoking.
Talking or texting on a cell phone.
Changing the radio station or CD.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Drivers make about 200 decisions for every mile they drive. It is important to focus all your attention on driving. Any other task can be a dangerous distraction.

questions.question: When you see a school bus stopped with its stop arm extended, you should:

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait.
Honk your horn before passing on the left.
Keep driving when you think most children have left the bus.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when you see a school bus with its stop arm extended. Do not move until the stop arm is pulled back in.

questions.question: Which of these commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Not paying attention while driving
Driving too fast for the conditions
Following other cars too closely
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of crashes. Not paying attention can cause you to hit other vehicles. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: Before turning, you should:

options.text: Use your turn signal.
Turn the steering wheel.
Speed up.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signal.
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal 3 to 4 seconds before you turn to help other drivers know your plans.

questions.question: A passenger in a moving car is not allowed to:

options.text: Have an open alcohol container.
Sleep.
Use a cell phone.
Use a map.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have an open alcohol container.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to have an open alcohol container in a moving vehicle on a public road. The driver can be punished for this.

questions.question: To change lanes safely, you should:

options.text: Check mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check mirrors, look over your shoulder for blind spots, then change lanes.
Signal, check mirrors, then change lanes.
Signal and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, look over your shoulder for blind spots, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal in the direction you want to go. Check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot and make sure no one is in the lane you want to enter. Only change lanes when it is safe.

questions.question: Alcohol causes:

options.text: Loss of focus.
Poor coordination.
Slower judgment.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol damages your vision, judgment, focus, and coordination.

questions.question: At an intersection with no signs or signals, you arrive at the same time as a car to your right. You should:

options.text: Speed up to get through first.
Slow down and let the car on your right go first.
Drive through and make the other car stop.
Honk and drive through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the car on your right go first.
questions.explanation: When two cars reach an intersection at the same time, the car on the right has the right-of-way. Wait for that car to pass safely before you go.

questions.question: Road rage and aggressive driving can be reduced by:

options.text: Leaving extra time to get where you are going.
Following posted speed limits.
Using turn signals.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Road rage is growing as more cars fill the roads. To prevent road rage, use your turn signals, follow speed limits, and give yourself plenty of time to drive.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while driving, you should:

options.text: Brake hard right away.
Keep the car straight and slow down by taking your foot off the gas.
Keep your current speed and drive straight.
Swerve back and forth to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the car straight and slow down by taking your foot off the gas.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel tight and keep the car going straight. Lift your foot off the gas pedal slowly. Do not brake until you have control of the car. When safe, brake gently and move to the side of the road.

questions.question: A seat belt should fit:

options.text: Loosely.
Snugly across your hip bones and lower belly.
Hidden under the seat.
So the buzzer or light turns off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snugly across your hip bones and lower belly.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should be snug across your hip bones and lower belly. The shoulder belt should rest comfortably so you can fit your fist between it and your chest.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Drink coffee.
Open your window.
Stop driving.
Turn on the radio.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop driving.
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is as dangerous as drunk driving. If you feel tired, stop driving.

questions.question: Night driving is harder than day driving because:

options.text: Cars overheat faster at night.
You cannot see as well in the dark.
It rains more at night.
You see more motorcycles at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as well in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead. Always use your headlights. Drive slowly enough to stop within the distance you can see.
